SOURCE: "AUTOSCIENTISTS: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation", Shanghua Gao*, Ada Fang*, Marinka Zitnik (Harvard). Preprint, arXiv:2605.28655v1 [cs.AI], 27 May 2026. Not peer reviewed. Code: github.com/mims-harvard/AutoScientists.

COVERAGE: 141,948 of 141,948 chars extracted. Body, appendices A-G and Tables S1-S9 all read. Skimmed: reference list (read only the entries credited below), Table S1, Table S7 per-task rows (only the first rows read), F.2 task descriptions, F.5 per-domain method lists, G.1 architecture details. I did not run the figures script. Captions below come from the extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Decentralised team beats single-agent Autoresearch on BioML-Bench under matched budget.
  number: 74.40 (6.20)% vs 66.07 (7.38)% mean leaderboard percentile, +8.33 points
  setup: 24 tasks. Claude Code agents on Claude Sonnet 4.6. 4 h on 1 H100 per task (16 h for imaging). 3 analysts + 6 experiment agents. Biomni was re-run under the same setting. The other baselines are published numbers from a different CPU-only 8 h protocol.
  quote: "AUTOSCIENTISTS achieves the highest mean (SE) leaderboard percentile among the evaluated systems, with 74.40 (6.20)% compared with 66.07 (7.38)% for Autoresearch, a gain of +8.33 leaderboard-percentile points."
  where: p6, Sec 4.2
- The gain is domain-dependent. Drug discovery gains most (n=9, 46.16 to 64.52). Protein engineering is tied and saturated (96.97 for both). Imaging gains are within the SE.
  number: imaging 45.75 (22.18) vs 39.60 (21.75); drug 64.52 (8.37) vs 46.16 (10.59)
  quote: "Drug Discovery(n= 9) 47.91 (10.77)2.2246.16 (10.59)2.00 64.52(8.37) 1.78"
  where: p6, Table 1
- On GPT nanochat it reaches the same loss in fewer experiments. This is per-experiment, not wall-clock.
  number: 34 vs 65 experiments to val_bpb ≈0.978 (1.9x)
  setup: 5-minute run on 1 H100 per experiment. Start val_bpb 0.998. Three self-formed teams (architecture, schedule, optimizer).
  quote: "AUTOSCIENTISTS reaches val_bpb≈0.978 in 34 experiments, while single-agent Autoresearch reaches the same value only after 65 experiments."
  where: p7
- From a strong champion, the team keeps finding improvements and the single agent finds none.
  number: 7 accepted of 93 experiments, val_bpb 0.9777 to 0.9730, vs 0 of 100
  setup: Both start from an AUTOSCIENTISTS champion after 50 experiments. Both get the same dead-end file EXPLORED.md. Single run each (n=1).
  quote: "Single-agent Autoresearch acceptszeroimprovements over 100 experiments, and its best attempt reaches val_bpb= 0.9783."
  where: p7. The first win (QK-norm order) was "never proposed by the single-agent loop in any of its 100 attempts".
- Seeded with Kermut (a strong ProteinGym baseline), it finds an extension, then the recipe is frozen and transfers.
  number: dev assay ACE2-Spike 0.747 to 0.840 Spearman (+12.5%). Full 217 assays 0.657 to 0.700 (+6.5%). MSE rises slightly, by 0.006.
  setup: 10 cycles, no human input, 1 H100. Tuned on a single assay. Result is a three-GP ensemble with quantile-warped targets and extra zero-shot features.
  quote: "improves the official average Spearman's ρ from 0.657 for Kermut to 0.700, an absolute gain of 0.043 and a 6.5% relative improvement."
  where: p8, Table 2
- Ablations: every removed component hurts on at least one task, and the damaging component differs by task.
  number: no-analyst on hERG AUROC 0.867 to 0.738. No cross-agent on plasma-protein binding Pearson 0.8729 to 0.7144. No self-org on GPT val_bpb 0.9777 to 0.9833. Independent agents on cell-cell communication odds ratio 0.924 to 0.435.
  setup: 4 tasks, one run per condition, same backend, compute and start.
  quote: "No single mechanism dominates across all four tasks and each removed component produces a AUTOSCIENTISTS that is dominated on at least one task."
  where: p9, Table 3
- Without shared state, agents duplicate work. Without self-organization, search stalls.
  number: 5 of 6 independent agents rediscovered the same first win (the batch-size reduction 2^19 to 2^18) in their first 2 experiments; best-of-population plateaus ~0.006 above full. No-cross-agent needed ~1.85x more experiments. No-self-org: 5 KEEPs, 0.9833, stalled after about 10 experiments.
  quote: "spending roughly a third of the budget on duplicates that the shared dead-ends ledger would have suppressed."
  where: p26, App D.2/D.4
- Crew size is task-dependent, and 14 agents is worse than 9 on every task tested.
  number: GPT val_bpb 0.9777 (n=2), 0.9778 (n=4), 0.9777 (n=9), 0.9821 (n=14). hERG percentile 14.3, 14.3, 85.7, 42.9. SPIKE-SARS2 Spearman 0.874, 0.835, 0.670, 0.506 (smaller crews win).
  quote: "At n=14, every task degrades relative to its best score in the table."
  where: p22-23, Table S3/B.2. Projected parallel speed-up of n=9 over n=2 is ~3.25x (≈26 vs ≈8 heartbeats). This is a projection: agents were run sequentially.
- Run-to-run stability on GPT is moderate.
  number: finals 0.9777, 0.9795, 0.9780; mean 0.9784, SD 0.0010. hERG 3 runs: 0.867, 0.830, 0.862 (mean 0.853, SD 0.020).
  where: App C and F.3
- Cost is higher than the main text suggests (see LIMITS).
  number: total $3984.7 vs $910.1 estimated, across 24 tasks
  quote: "Total 0.153 35.5 266.1 6184.5 3984.7" (AUTOSCIENTISTS columns, Table S8) and "Total 0.024 15.7 21.9 1807.5 910.1" (Autoresearch columns)
  where: p36-37, Table S8

MECHANISM (for the topology note; all in Sec 3 and App A)
- No orchestrator. Coordination goes through a shared state S: champion p*, experiment log L, forum F, per-team queues Q_k and dead-end registries D_k.
- Roles: analysts propose experiments, experiment agents execute them. Each agent is a stateless LLM session woken by a deterministic monitor loop (heartbeat), with identity and memory files.
- Teams form through a discussion phase. It ends on a majority [DISCUSS-DONE] vote. The "alphabetically-last analyst" writes the roster as a tie-breaker, and "the system has no privileged consolidator agent".
- Reorganisation is triggered by stagnation. Example: "no improvement in the last 10 experiments". Create, merge, split and retire changes need endorsement from the affected teams.
- Queue claims use optimistic locking on a version token.
- Noise-aware promotion gate: promote if Δ > 2σ. Re-run on a second seed if 0 < Δ ≤ 2σ. Reject otherwise. σ is pooled from duplicate-seed pairs, calibrated once n≥3 pairs exist, and locked at 5 pairs. This prevents "champion pollution".
- Analyst proposals are ranked by mean effect size per (axis, direction). Directions tried fewer than 3 times get an exploration bonus. An "ambition quota" and diversity rules apply, and a post-KEEP step asks which property made the win work.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Sec 5): it is not more LLM-call efficient. "uses more LLM tokens than Autoresearch... though within the same order of magnitude". Table S8 totals show about 4.4x the cost, so I flag "same order of magnitude" as generous.
- BioML-Bench runs were limited to one H100 per task, so GPU experiments ran sequentially. The paper says this "does not fully exercise" parallelism. Scaling with GPUs is untested. The agent count is fixed in advance.
- Speed-ups are per-experiment, not wall-clock. Parallel wall-clock figures are projected, because the agents were executed iteratively.
- Mostly single runs. Ablations are n=1. The authors note for no-analyst that "the gap to the full system is not statistically supported". The full system never beat Autoresearch's own run in the ablation anchor plots: Fig S4 lists autoresearch 0.9773 (15 KEEPs / 83 exps) vs full 0.9777 (71 exps). Table S2 says Autoresearch reaches 0.9790 at 50 experiments. So the advantage depends on the budget window.
- Only one backbone model (Claude Sonnet 4.6), and the Autoresearch baseline uses the same one. The paper claims "LLM-agnostic" without testing other models.
- BioML-Bench comparison is mixed. Other baselines (AIDE, MLAgentBench, STELLA) are published CPU-only 8 h numbers. Only Biomni and Autoresearch share the hardware setting. Standard errors are large (SE 8 to 22 points per domain).
- Protein engineering is saturated (tie at 96.97). The Kermut recipe was tuned on one assay. MSE got slightly worse. The SPIKE assay improvement in the dev set is not an out-of-sample result, but the 217-assay transfer is.
- The paper does not compare against other decentralised or multi-agent frameworks as baselines (for example CORAL, InternAgent, Virtual Lab, debate). The main comparison is single-agent Autoresearch and Biomni. It does not test a central-planner multi-agent control with the same number of agents and roles, so topology effects are confounded with agent count and shared state.
- Dates: Autoresearch (Karpathy, 2026) is a very recent GitHub repo.

- Karpathy, Autoresearch, GitHub 2026 (baseline and the nanochat benchmark).
- Jiang et al., AIDE, arXiv:2502.13138, 2025.
- Miller et al., BioML-bench, bioRxiv 2025.
- Huang et al., Biomni, bioRxiv 2025. Jin et al., STELLA, bioRxiv 2026.
- Groth et al., Kermut, NeurIPS (as printed, editors Globerson et al.).
- Contrast cases for topology: Du et al., multiagent debate, ICML 2024; Chen et al., ReConcile, arXiv 2309.13007 (2024); Swanson et al., Virtual Lab (PI-scientist-critic), Nature 646, 2025; CORAL (Qu et al., arXiv:2604.01658, 2026); InternAgent-1.5 (arXiv 2602...).
- Multi-agent caveats they cite: Kim et al., "Towards a science of scaling agent systems", arXiv:2512.08296, 2025; Pappu et al., "Multi-agent teams hold experts back", arXiv:2602.01011, 2026.

CODE (verbatim, Eq. 1 and 2, p21)
promote(p') = true if Δ > Mσ; confirm(p', seed 2) if 0 < Δ ≤ Mσ; false if Δ ≤ 0   (M = 2)
σ = sqrt( (1/2n) Σ (ℓ1,i − ℓ2,i)² )   (pooled within-pair SD, n≥3 pairs, locked at 5)

FIGURES
- Figure 1 (p2): "Self-organizing agent teams for long-running experimentation. Overview of AUTOSCIENTISTS. Agents identify promising research directions, organize into teams, and execute experiments in parallel." Shows the shared-state blackboard (champion, experiment log, forum, team queues, dead ends) and the stagnation-triggered reorganisation loop. It is the single best picture of the topology for the note. Fig 4 (p8, best val_bpb curves, 34 vs 65 experiments) is the evidence figure.

- Table S3 caption says "same five tasks as Table 3" but it shows three tasks, and Table 3 has four. I did not resolve this.
